   \[
   \text{Time (in hours)} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Speed}} = \frac{30 \text{ miles}}{60 \text{ mph}} = 0.5 \text{ hours}
   \]

2. Convert the time from hours to seconds:
   - There are 60 minutes in an hour.
   - There are 60 seconds in a minute.
   \[
   \text{Total seconds} = 0.5 \text{ hours} \times 60 \text{ minutes/hour} \times 60 \text{ seconds/minute}
   \]
   \[
   0.5 \times 60 = 30 \text{ minutes}
   \]
   \[
   30 \times 60 = 1800 \text{ seconds}
   \]

Thus, the train takes \boxed{1800} seconds to travel 30 miles.
